title: Beta API key rotation + end of free keys — announcement draft (scratch)
content:
Purpose:
- Quick scratchpad for a customer-facing announcement + internal comms about rotating beta API keys and sunsetting the unlimited/free trial keys. Intended audience: growth/product comms, support, eng on-call, legal for final review.

TL;DR (for execs):
- We will rotate all 'beta' API keys and retire the legacy free keys on 2026-04-15.
- Customers will get a single 30-day window to migrate to new keys with improved quota controls and optional auto-rotate.
- Goal: reduce abuse, improve predictability of throttling, and align billing/security posture ahead of GA.

Why now (notes to self):
- Rising abuse vectors: automated scraping + credential stuffing on low-friction beta keys.
- Cost volatility: a small fraction of free-key users are consuming disproportionate compute.
- Security: ability to enforce key-level rotation and enforce KMS-backed key storage on new keys.
- Product readiness: new onboarding flow + metered quotas are in place (see CONF-REDWOOD-1249).

High-level customer-facing message (subject lines and short variants):
- Subject (email): "Important: Upcoming API key rotation & beta key retirement (action recommended)"
- Slack/console banner short: "API key rotation scheduled — check your inbox for migration steps"

Suggested announcement email (editable):
Hi <Customer name>,

We’re reaching out to let you know that on 2026-04-15 we’ll rotate all legacy beta API keys and retire the older free keys. This change is part of our ongoing effort to improve platform security and make usage more predictable for everyone.

What this means for you:
- Action: Generate a new key in the Console by 2026-04-15. You’ll have a 30-day migration window.
- No disruption: If you create a new key before the deadline, your traffic will continue uninterrupted. After the deadline, requests using legacy keys will receive a 401/403 and a short response directing you to rotate.
- New benefits: the new key system supports per-key quotas, optional automatic rotation, and KMS-backed secret storage for private deployments.

Need help? Reply to this email or open a support ticket. We’ll also post step-by-step migration docs and a one-click rotate button in the Console.

Thanks,
The Redwood Inference team

Slack/Console banner copy (short):
We’re rotating legacy beta keys and retiring free keys on 2026-04-15. Create a new key in Console to avoid interruptions. Details in your inbox.

Internal all-hands talking points (for PM/Eng leads):
- Quick baseline: This is not a rate-limit change; it’s an identity/credential rotation + sunsetting of the legacy free-key type.
- Why: Security + abuse + cost predictability. We’ve seen spikes from bot farms using leaked keys; rotating and enforcing per-key quotas reduces blast radius.
- Impact estimates: ~12k active free keys; ~9% of active traffic today originates from keys flagged as legacy/free. Most users are low-volume; small set of heavy users will be asked to convert to paid/committed flows.
- Timeline: 2026-03-16 internal communications -> 2026-03-23 public blog post -> 2026-04-15 rotation & retirement.
- Escalation path: Support -> Solutions Eng -> On-call SRE -> Product lead. Use JIRA API-8890 for triage tags.

Anticipated customer questions & suggested responses (Q&A):
Q: Will my app break?
A: If you rotate before 2026-04-15, no. After the deadline, old keys will be rejected and you’ll need a new key. Provide step-by-step migration and code snippets in the help center.

Q: Why are you retiring free keys?
A: Free keys were intended for low-friction evaluation. Over time they became an abuse vector and are costly at scale. New keys offer better controls and optional billing/commitment options.

Q: I can’t pay right now — will you cut me off?
A: No immediate billing changes. The rotation is about credentials. We’ll offer a 30-day migration window and a special 60-day hardship extension on request; support will triage case-by-case.

Q: Will this affect Private/VPC customers?
A: Private deployments that use customer-managed keys are unaffected by the Console rotation; we’ll provide targeted comms for Private customers clarifying no action required unless they use the legacy cloud-managed beta keys.

Q: What about rate limits and quotas?
A: New keys support per-key quotas. We will preserve existing rate-limit defaults for migrated accounts unless they choose to opt into lower/higher tiers.

Operational checklist (to do before public blog):
- [ ] Finalize public blog + support article (owner: content).
- [ ] Add Console banner and in-console key generator + one-click migrate (owner: Console eng).
- [ ] Prepare support playbook with canned responses and escalation flow (owner: support lead).
- [ ] Security review sign-off for rotation plan & KMS integration (owner: security).
- [ ] Billing/product cadence for heavy users transition options (owner: growth/product).
- [ ] Dry run in staging: rotate 100 keys and verify failover behaviors (owner: SRE/QA).

Notes to self / risks to surface:
- Be explicit about 401 vs 403 semantics in server responses; signal migration URL in response body to improve UX.
- Consider a short-lived grace proxy (sends warning header but allows calls for 48 hours) — requires engineering resources and risk review.
- Watch for social amplification: coordinate with comms/time-of-day to reduce churn on a Friday.

Follow-ups after announcement (post-migration metrics):
- Retention of migrated users, percent traffic blocked, number of support tickets, abuse reduction (blocked IPs), and daily cost delta.

Draft checklist for final sign-off meeting (one-pager):
- Migration docs ready and linked in email.
- Console buttons visible in beta accounts.
- Support playbook uploaded to internal KB.
- Legal notified re: TOS updates if we change billing behavior.
- Exec comms scheduled for 24h before rotation.

-- end of scratchpad --

Notes: keep as a lightweight working doc; will iterate with Support + Console + Security.
